anti_overlap: Do NOT review benchmark governance, devrel, or eval methodology directly
Do NOT review clinical-trial adaptive design, journal pre-registration, or sports-league rules
Do NOT review wine-appellation aging, cheese aging, cathedral-construction commitment arcs (already claimed)
Stay focused on the irreversibility-and-maturation-sequencing frame; do not drift into general 'launch strategy'
decision_lens: Once this v0.1-preview is shipped under DRAFT-protocol labels and the 60-day clock starts, what early decisions are silently committing the project to a flavor it can't develop out of — and which decisions are still reversible enough to defer?
distance_rationale: A software engineer reviewing a benchmark-launch PRD would never consult a centuries-old fermentation craft because the temporal scales feel incomparable — but irreversibility-under-public-witness is the exact same problem at both scales.
expected_isomorphisms: Maillard reactions are the canonical example of chemistry that cannot be run backwards: once a melanoidin forms in a sauce, it's a permanent constituent that all future flavor must develop around. Public scorecards under v0.1-preview labeling are structurally identical: once published with named dimensions and named models, those publications become permanent constituents of the project's leaderboard reputation that LOCKED-protocol must develop around, not replace. The sauce-maker's discipline of sequencing reversible vs. irreversible choices (you can add more salt later; you cannot un-brown) maps directly onto the discipline a single-developer benchmark needs to sequence what to publish and what to defer until LOCK.
focus: Audits whether the project's irreversible commitments (DRAFT-protocol labeling, 60-day kill-gate, public scorecards under v0.1-preview) are sequenced such that early choices don't foreclose the late-stage character the project is supposed to develop.
name: fd-maillard-irreversibility-arc
persona: Apply the perspective of a long-aged sauce-maker (think a 25-year colatura di alici master or a 50-year soy mash steward) — they care that each irreversible step in the aging arc develops rather than stalls the final character, measure the maturation by how non-volatile compounds compound (Maillard browning, melanoidin formation, peptide cleavage), and flag any early choice that locks the batch into a flavor trajectory the maturation cannot escape.
review_areas: v0.1-preview labeling — Maillard reactions are irreversible; once browning starts, you can't 'un-brown.' Does shipping public scorecards labeled 'preview against DRAFT protocol' commit the project to a public reputation that protocol-LOCK can't later override, or is the labeling itself a shield that preserves optionality?

60-day falsification gate — long-aged sauces have a window where the batch is still 'savable' and a point of no return where you commit to the full age. Is 60 days the right window, or does the F1-cultural-fit-validation-gate already burn most of the optionality before engineering starts?

PROTOCOL.md DRAFT lock-transition (paused as shadow-work-nzcy) — is the pause itself an aging step that develops the protocol, or is it a stall where unwanted flavors (community confusion, scorecard incompatibility) develop unchecked?

Persistent run history (`runs.jsonl`) and re-scoring path (F5) — Maillard products are stable; once a melanoidin forms it's a permanent constituent of the sauce. Are early-bench runs becoming permanent constituents of the leaderboard reputation, even if scoring is later corrected?

Distribution sequencing (registry → Discord post → HuggingFace Spaces → cross-posts) — order of releases matters in fermentation; the wrong order produces wrong character. Does the PRD's distribution order develop the right reputation arc, or does it expose the project to feedback that locks early-stage flavors?

Scorecard format (4 named dimensions, locked formula) — once a dimension is named in public, the name itself becomes part of the recipe. Are the 4 dimension names ones the project can live with for years, or are they v0.1 flavors that will grate in the LOCKED protocol?

severity_examples.issue: Public scorecards under v0.1-preview that name specific commercial models (Claude 4.7, GPT-5) by score will be screenshotted and propagate beyond the 'preview' caveat — once Maillard fires, the browning is in the sauce. The PRD needs an explicit irreversibility audit on which v0.1 publications are 'add salt' (reversible) and which are 'add heat' (not). Required to exit the gate.

The 60-day kill-gate is positioned as a binary go/no-go, but real maturation has a third state: 'the batch developed, just into a different sauce than planned.' The gate lacks a YELLOW outcome equivalent to the F1 cultural-fit verdict — what if the audience hypothesis partially confirms? Degrades the gate's ability to capture the realistic mid-state outcome.
Dimension names locked at v0.1 are not flagged as a separately-irreversible commitment from the scoring formula; renaming a dimension after publication is harder than re-tuning its weight.

source_domain: Long-aged fermented sauce maturation (e.g., 25-year colatura di alici, 50-year aged soy mash, traditional balsamic) — a craft tradition where Maillard reactions, melanoidin formation, and peptide development are individually irreversible and the master must sequence early choices (salt level, vessel material, stir rhythm) such that decades-later flavor character is reachable from the early state
success_hints: Build an irreversibility ledger: list every v1 commitment (binary release tags, public dimension names, model identities in scorecards, registry listing copy) and classify each as REVERSIBLE / EXPENSIVE-TO-REVERSE / IRREVERSIBLE

Add a YELLOW gate-outcome to the 60-day falsification gate that maps to 'the project developed differently than planned but the batch is salvageable' — define what that pivot looks like before the clock starts

Defer naming-decisions on dimensions and scorecard format until F1 cultural-fit returns GREEN/YELLOW; what reads as alignment-jargon in the Nous community may need re-flavoring before public scorecard exposure
task_context: Reviewing a v1 PRD for an alignment benchmark shipping under DRAFT-protocol labeling with a 60-day falsification gate. Focus on which early commitments are quietly irreversible and whether the project's maturation arc is well-sequenced.
